territorial_scope.description: Applies to autonomous vehicles operated on public roads in California, as stated in the amended Vehicle Code provisions.

evidence.quote: The autonomous vehicle is being operated on roads in this state solely by employees, contractors, or other persons designated by the manufacturer

summary.short: California statute amending the Vehicle Code so that autonomous vehicles may be tested and deployed on public roads only under Department of Motor Vehicles approval, insurance and certification requirements, with emergency-response duties for manufacturers from July 1, 2026.
summary.long: Amends Vehicle Code section 38750 and adds sections 38751, 38752 and 38753. Defines autonomous technology, autonomous vehicles (SAE Level 3, 4 or 5), manufacturer and operator. Testing on public roads is allowed by designated personnel with a licensed driver seated in the driver's seat, provided the manufacturer holds 5 million dollars in insurance, surety bond or self-insurance. Other operation requires the department's approval of the manufacturer's application, which must include certifications on engagement mechanisms, visual indicators, failure alerts, operator takeover, federal safety standards, and at least 30 seconds of read-only sensor data retained for three years after a collision. The department adopts regulations, may impose additional requirements (including for vehicles without a driver), and must post public notice 30 days before approvals under the regulations. Federal NHTSA regulations prevail in conflict. Manufacturers must give purchasers a written disclosure of collected information and the department may assess a cost-recovery fee. From January 1, 2030, light vehicles of model year 2031 or later may operate only under a deployment permit if zero-emission. Section 38751 (operative July 1, 2026) requires an emergency telephone line answered within 30 seconds, two-way communication devices, remote operators able to immobilize vehicles, law enforcement override access with training, and direction to leave an area within two minutes of an emergency geofencing message. Section 38752 lets peace officers issue notices of autonomous vehicle noncompliance, which manufacturers must provide to the department within 72 hours; it is inoperative until regulations are adopted.

notes: The document contains no bill number or enactment record; AB 1777 appears only in registry metadata. Target instrument IDs are blank because no registry IDs were given. Operative dates differ: § 38751 becomes operative 1 July 2026 (§ 38751(g)); § 38750(i) applies from 1 January 2030, and rulemaking for it may not start before 1 January 2027; § 38752 is not operative until the department issues regulations on notices (§ 38752(e)). Section 38751(b)(1)(A) refers to a 'testing permit or deployment permit issued by the department'; the text does not define a testing permit.

“Autonomous technology” means technology that has the capability to drive a vehicle without the active physical control or monitoring by a human operator.
“Autonomous vehicle” means any vehicle equipped with autonomous technology that has been integrated into that vehicle that meets the definition of Level 3, Level 4, or Level 5

definitions.term: Autonomous vehicle (exclusion of collision avoidance and driver assistance vehicles)

evidence.quote: An autonomous vehicle does not include a vehicle that is equipped with one or more collision avoidance systems
An “operator” of an autonomous vehicle is the person who is seated in the driver’s seat, or, if there is no person in the driver’s seat, causes the autonomous technology to engage.

obligations.summary: Before testing in California, the manufacturer performing testing must hold insurance, a surety bond or proof of self-insurance of $5,000,000 and provide evidence to the department. The application certifications in subdivision (c)(3) repeat the same insurance requirement.
obligations.applies_from: Prior to the start of testing in this state
obligations.conditional_on: Testing on public roads under subdivision (b)

evidence.quote: the manufacturer performing the testing shall obtain an instrument of insurance, surety bond, or proof of self-insurance in the amount of five million dollars ($5,000,000)

obligations.summary: During testing, the driver (the operator) must sit in the driver's seat, monitor safe operation and be able to take immediate manual control. The vehicle may be operated for testing only by employees, contractors or persons designated by the manufacturer.
obligations.conditional_on: Autonomous vehicle operated on public roads for testing under subdivision (b)

evidence.quote: The driver shall be seated in the driver’s seat, monitoring the safe operation of the autonomous vehicle

obligations.summary: Outside testing, an autonomous vehicle may not operate on public roads until the manufacturer submits an application that the department approves under its regulations. The application must contain the certifications in subdivision (c)(1) to (c)(3).

evidence.quote: until the manufacturer submits an application to the department

obligations.summary: The manufacturer must certify that the vehicle has an easily accessible engage/disengage mechanism, a cabin indicator of engagement, and an alert system for technology failure, which requires operator takeover or a complete stop. It must also certify operator override by brake, accelerator or steering, and compliance with federal and state safety standards.

evidence.quote: The autonomous vehicle has a system to safely alert the operator if an autonomous technology failure is detected while the autonomous technology is engaged

obligations.summary: The vehicle must have a separate read-only mechanism that captures and stores autonomous technology sensor data for at least 30 seconds before a collision, retained until extracted by an external device. The data must be preserved for three years after the collision.

evidence.quote: The data shall be preserved for three years after the date of the collision.

obligations.summary: The application must certify that the manufacturer has tested the autonomous technology on public roads and complied with any testing standards the department has set.

evidence.quote: A certification that the manufacturer has tested the autonomous technology on public roads

obligations.summary: The department must adopt regulations on evidence of insurance, the application process and notices of noncompliance. Under subdivisions (d)(2) and (d)(3) it must also set testing, equipment and performance standards, and may adopt further requirements such as deployment limits and license rules.

evidence.quote: The department shall adopt regulations setting forth requirements for the submission of evidence of insurance, surety bond, or self-insurance

obligations.summary: The department must hold public hearings before adopting any regulation on operating an autonomous vehicle without a driver inside the vehicle.
obligations.conditional_on: Regulation applicable to operation of an autonomous vehicle without the presence of a driver inside the vehicle

evidence.quote: The department shall hold public hearings on the adoption of any regulation applicable to the operation of an autonomous vehicle without the presence of a driver inside the vehicle.

obligations.summary: The department must approve a manufacturer's application if it finds that the applicant has submitted all required information and testing and complied with the regulations. For driverless vehicles, it may impose additional requirements or require a driver.
obligations.conditional_on: Application submitted under subdivision (c) and the department finds that the applicant has complied with the requirements

evidence.quote: The department shall approve an application submitted by a manufacturer pursuant to subdivision (c) if it finds that the applicant has submitted all information

obligations.summary: After adopting the regulations under subdivision (d), the department must post a public notice on its website. It may not approve an application under those regulations until 30 days after the notice.
obligations.conditional_on: Department adopts regulations required by subdivision (d)

evidence.quote: The department shall post a public notice on its internet website when it adopts the regulations required by subdivision (d).

obligations.summary: The manufacturer of the autonomous technology must give the purchaser of an autonomous vehicle a written disclosure describing what information the installed technology collects.

evidence.quote: shall provide a written disclosure to the purchaser of an autonomous vehicle

obligations.summary: The department may adopt regulations to charge manufacturers that apply to operate autonomous vehicles a fee sufficient to recover its reasonable costs.
obligations.conditional_on: Manufacturer submits an application under subdivision (c)

evidence.quote: The department may promulgate regulations to assess a fee upon a manufacturer that submits an application

obligations.summary: Certain light autonomous vehicles (model year 2031 or later, gross vehicle weight rating under 8,501 pounds) may operate only under a deployment permit, and only if they are zero-emission vehicles.
obligations.conditional_on: To the extent authorized by federal law; model year 2031 or later; gross vehicle weight rating less than 8,501 pounds; zero-emission vehicle as defined in Health and Safety Code § 44258

evidence.quote: shall only be operated pursuant to a deployment permit

obligations.summary: The manufacturer must keep a dedicated emergency telephone line staffed around the clock, answer calls within 30 seconds through a remote human operator who can immobilize or move the vehicle, and provide a two-way voice device that reaches that operator within 30 seconds. It must also give law enforcement and firefighters access to any override system and train them on it.

evidence.quote: shall maintain a dedicated emergency response telephone line that is available for emergency response officials during all hours when an autonomous vehicle is on a public road
